$comment: Machine-readable handoff for a second agent working on Big Brain. Prose version: HANDOFF.md

project.name: Big Brain
project.oneLiner: A drop-anything reference inbox: save a link, image, or note from anywhere; find it later.

owner.name: Rader
owner.context: Project-based film/TV and commercial work. Captures visual references (furniture, props, textures, lighting, wardrobe, locations) while on his feet, on set, often with poor signal.

project.visibility: public — never paste secrets into chat windows or committed files

stack.language: JavaScript, no framework, no build step
stack.ui: Self-contained HTML pages served as template literals from the Worker
stack.tests: Plain Node scripts, no test framework

dataModel.idScheme: reverse-timestamp + random, so a plain key-prefix list returns newest-first with cursor paging

auth.model: single shared secret, single user, no accounts
auth.clientStorage: localStorage + IndexedDB (the service worker can only read IndexedDB)

endpoints.purpose: save a link/note (JSON) or file (raw bytes)
delete a ref and its blob
raw bytes; the random key is the capability
gallery: thumbnails, filter chips, search, edit, delete, export
connect a device, per-platform share-sheet instructions

shipped: Auto-categorization by content-type, file extension, and a domain ruleset
Open Graph scraping for saved links (title, description, thumbnail)
Gallery with thumbnails, category chips, full-text search, edit, delete, NDJSON export/import
Installable PWA with a share_target — Big Brain is in the phone's share sheet
iOS Shortcut recipe, pre-filled with the real URL and token
Offline app shell and a sync-later queue in IndexedDB
Dependency-free local dev server, no Cloudflare account needed

wanted.title: Semantic search
wanted.detail: 'that rust-colored velvet armchair' should find the thing even though those words appear nowhere in the title.
wanted.guidance: Prefer the cheapest approach that works at this scale. Embeddings in KV with brute-force cosine over a few thousand items is probably fine — say where that breaks down. Cloudflare Workers AI runs embeddings inside the Worker with no external call; Vectorize is the same-account upgrade path.

wanted.title: Auto-tagging images
wanted.detail: A vision model tags a saved photo with material, color, era, and object type, in set-decoration vocabulary rather than generic alt-text.
wanted.guidance: Use a small/cheap vision model for the bulk pass, not a frontier model. Needs the controlled vocabulary from task queue item 1.

wanted.title: Boards / projects
wanted.detail: Group refs into a named project (work is project-based, each with a codename), and export a board as a PDF or shareable link to send a director or producer.

wanted.title: Dupe detection
wanted.detail: The same chair saved from four different sites should collapse into one.

wanted.title: Weekly digest
wanted.detail: 'Here's what you saved this week, grouped by theme.'

constraints: Cloudflare Workers runtime: no Node built-ins, no filesystem, per-request CPU limits
KV values capped at 25 MB; KV is eventually consistent
No build step — plain JS that a browser or the Workers runtime runs as-is
Do not introduce React, TypeScript, or a bundler
Single user — do not design for multi-tenancy
Stay on or near Cloudflare's free tier
Match the existing style: small focused modules, comments explaining why, plain Node test scripts

rulesOfEngagement.reason: One driver per branch. Claude Code integrates the output and runs the tests. Two agents editing the same files produces conflicts.
rulesOfEngagement.gate: npm test must pass before anything is pushed

taskQueue.title: Set-dec tagging vocabulary + vision prompt + eval set
taskQueue.deliverable: a single JSON object: facets (object, material, era, color, finish, style, use), a vision_prompt, and 25 eval cases

taskQueue.title: Adversarial review of the semantic-search plan
taskQueue.prerequisite: Claude Code writes the plan first

taskQueue.title: Board / PDF layout options for client-facing exports

toolRouting.$comment: Which work is worth sending where, by cost and capability.

avoid: bulk image tagging — frontier pricing for a job a small model does as well

smallVisionModel.why: comparable quality on 'tag this chair', roughly 10-20x cheaper

candidates: Cloudflare Workers AI (runs inside the Worker, no external call)
embeddings.note: Not a job for a chat model.

use: anything that must run the tests

openQuestions: Not yet deployed — the Worker URL is unknown until `npm run setup` is run.
No real corpus yet, so tasks 3 and 4 above cannot be tuned against real data.
